nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What type of methodology was applied in the assessment focused on residue management at the farm?
nodes.answer: The assessment applied consequential life cycle assessment (LCA) methodology.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and its purpose?
nodes.answer: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is an internationally standardized method used to quantify the potential environmental impacts of products by considering their full life cycle.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_002
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What is the ISO standard mentioned for Life Cycle Assessment?
nodes.answer: The ISO standard mentioned for Life Cycle Assessment is ISO 14040, established in 2006.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_003
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What are the four main steps of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)?
nodes.answer: The four main steps of LCA are goal and scope definition, Life Cycle Inventory (LCI), Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA), and interpretation of results.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the main purpose of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main purpose of LCA is to provide a standardized methodology that guarantees rigour and uniformity in calculating environmental impacts, supporting the evaluation of alternative production pathways, and aiding in informed decision-making processes within the circular economy.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_005
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is the scope of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)?
nodes.answer: LCA assesses systems "cradle-to-grave," from gathering materials from the earth to returning materials to the earth.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_006
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the purpose of the document "Towards a Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment" by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)?
nodes.answer: The document aims to provide guidance on conducting life cycle sustainability assessments, considering social, environmental, and economic factors.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How is the inventory of a particular environmental flow calculated in the LCD phase of Life Cycle Assessment?
nodes.answer: The inventory of a particular environmental flow is calculated by subtracting the environmental factor associated with the input or output from the quantity of the process input or output, as shown in Equation (11).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the use of LCA (Life Cycle Assessment) help guide companies in sustainable decision-making?
nodes.answer: LCA serves as a tool to quantify the environmental impacts of different stages in the product lifecycle, guiding companies in sustainable decision-making.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green manufacturing methods|Life cycle assessment_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some key lessons learned from case studies in life cycle sustainability assessment?
nodes.answer: Case studies in life cycle sustainability assessment provide valuable insights into the environmental impacts of products or processes, helping to identify areas for improvement and sustainable practices.
